data.why: data/raw/ is gitignored and not shipped; the dashboard's CSV-replay sidebar lists whatever files sit in data/raw/ (via find_csv_files(DATASET_DIR)), so three small synthetic recordings matching the documented 5-column Muse schema (timestamps, TP9, AF7, AF8, TP10, Right AUX) and the subject<id>-<state>-<trial>.csv naming convention were written there so the selectbox is populated and each file's band-power mix is tuned (low/mid/high alpha vs beta amplitude) to plausibly land in the concentrating/neutral/relaxed region of the already-committed config/thresholds.yaml.

goals: Load a recorded EEG CSV and watch the dashboard replay it as a live stream of TP9/AF7/AF8/TP10 traces.
Observe the rule-based decision engine classify successive 4-second windows into Concentrating, Neutral or Relaxed with a confidence score.
Inspect which individual band-power features (e.g. TP10_alpha, TP9_delta) drove a given classification and by how much, via the decision log and statistics panel.
Compare classification behavior across recordings of different labeled cognitive states to judge whether the spectral signatures separate the states as claimed.
Check electrode/channel signal quality and connection status before trusting a window's classification.
Switch between CSV replay and a live Muse/LSL connection mode to understand how the same pipeline would run online.

review.summary: The tree correctly frames the dashboard as the online stage of a calibrated, explainable EEG state classifier: choose a source, check the signal, watch the window labels, compare labelled recordings. Its evidence and six features mostly hold up. It needs fixes before filing: it calls synthetic seed data built-in, it wrongly says the crashed decision log holds per-feature explanations, it claims a Decision-age tooltip that does not exist, and it leaves out the decision-history task and feature.
